transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-05
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Ramos (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Tomas Lee (Redwood Product), Samir Patel (Cobalt CTO), Maya Chen (Lead SRE), Jordan Lee (Security), Priya Rao (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be short):
Redwood demo of request storage toggles and telemetry escrow/workflow. Walkthrough of Console toggles, API flags, and Optimize recommendations for minimizing token logging while preserving debug telemetry. Customer concerns: auditability, SOC2/KMS, retention for debugging vs compliance, ability to escrow/ship telemetry to third party.

Topics: console request-storage toggles; per-route storage policies; PII redaction; ephemeral vs persisted logs; telemetry escrow for audits; RBAC + KMS access controls; performance impact of retention.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex (Redwood): All right good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 45 minutes on the calendar, we'll try to cover the console toggles, the API flags, and show a short Optimize run. Priya and Tomas from our side will jump into the deep bits. Samir, do you want to kick off with what you want from the session?
[00:18] Samir (Cobalt): Yeah thanks Alex, uh main thing for us is we operate in regulated infra, so we need to know how telemetry and request logs are handled. Specifically: can we turn off request storage per route, who can access stored requests, and if we need to hand over telemetry to auditors can we escrow it without exposing customer PII.
[00:35] Priya (Redwood): Absolutely. We'll show the per-route toggles, the ephemeral mode, and the escrow flow. Quick note, some of the naming in the console UI is a bit different from the docs, you might see "request-storage" vs "telemetry-archive" labels depending on your tenancy.
[00:50] Maya (Cobalt): That's fine, just point it out. Also curious about encryption at rest — we use a KMS and HSM for our keys. How does Redwood integrate?
[01:05] Tomas (Redwood): We support customer-managed keys via KMS and HSM integrations, you can rotate keys, and audit key usage. The telemetry egress uses envelope encryption so auditors can decrypt a separate escrow bundle with a separate key — long story short we can do escrow without exposing your production keys.
[01:22] Jordan (Cobalt - Security): When you say escrow bundle, is that stored in your hosted vault or do we control the target? We need chain-of-custody for the audit artifacts.
[01:35] Alex (Redwood): Good question. We provide two options: 1) Redwood-managed escrow where we put a time-limited package in an S3-compatible bucket owned by Redwood and ship a delivery manifest, or 2) tenant-managed escrow where we push an encrypted bundle to a bucket in your account (preferred for high-compliance customers). We can demo option 2 today.
[01:55] Samir (Cobalt): Option 2 sounds better. Show us how to configure that.
[02:05] Priya (Redwood): Sure. I'll share my screen and open the Console. Heads-up: this is a staging tenant, labels might slightly vary.
[02:20] [screen share starts - Console view]
[02:32] Priya (Redwood): Here on the left nav, there's an "Observability" section. Under the Request Storage page you can set a global default—persist, ephemeral, or escrow-only. Then there's a per-route override so you can mark specific API routes as ephemeral (for example, PII-sensitive endpoints).
[02:50] Samir: Can we set a retention window too? Like keep persisted logs for 30 days but artifacts for 7 years for legal hold?
[03:05] Priya: Yes, retention windows are configurable per-policy. There's also a "legal-hold" flag which pins data beyond the window until an explicit release. Note that longer retention has cost and, depending on the model, some performance impact on the KV cache warm-up if you keep long-term request payload references.
[03:27] Maya: You said performance impact. Quantify it — what's the token-latency delta if we enable persisted request storage for high QPS endpoints?
[03:40] Tomas: In our internal tests, enabling persistent request indexing added ~6-12ms median on token latency for small seq lengths, but it depends on indexing metadata and the amount of post-processing (e.g., PII redaction pipelines). We can run a short benchmark with your sample traffic to provide exact numbers.
[03:58] Jordan: What about the PII redaction step — is it sync or async? We need guarantees that PII doesn't hit persistent storage unredacted.
[04:12] Priya: We have two modes: sync redaction applied at ingest (recommended for high-compliance routes) and async redaction where raw telemetry is stored for a short window while the redaction pipeline runs, then replaced. The async path is only for customers who explicitly opt-in; default for regulated customers is sync redaction.
[04:32] Samir: Okay show the sync config.
[04:40] [00:04:40 - Console] Priya: On this policy page you can toggle "Apply PII redaction at ingest" and select predefined patterns (SSN, email, phone, credit card) or upload custom regex sets. Warning — regex can be brittle, we offer an ML-backed PII classifier as well which is higher recall but may add a small processing cost.
[05:00] Priya: I'll flip to the API flags next. The SDKs have a request param "store_requests": true|false and "redaction_mode": "sync"|"async". For curl it's just a header: X-Redwood-Store: none|persist|escrow.
[05:18] Maya: If a route is marked ephemeral at the console level, but the SDK header requests persist, which wins?
[05:30] Tomas: Policy precedence is: tenant policy > route policy > request header. So admin-set tenancy rules will override client headers. We built that deliberately to prevent accidental client-side overrides.
[05:45] Jordan: Auditing access — who can pull persisted requests? Is there RBAC integrated with our SSO?
[05:58] Alex: Yes, we tie RBAC to SAML SSO. Roles map to Console permissions. There's an "auditor" role with read-only access to escrow bundles and a separate "forensics" role which can request a one-time decrypt with an approval workflow. All actions are logged in the audit trail with immutable entries.
[06:15] Samir: Great. Can you show a sample audit log entry?
[06:22] [06:22] Priya (Redwood): Here's an entry: "2027-09-22T14:23:12Z user:jordan.lee action:download_escrow bundle_id:eb-345 status:approved by:compliance@cobalt". Note sometimes the auto-transcription of our console shows user emails slightly different as they are masked in the UI.
[06:45] Maya: On the escrow download, does the bundle include raw request payloads? We need to ensure PII is redacted or that the bundle is encrypted with an escrow key we control.
[06:58] Priya: If tenant-managed escrow is configured, the bundle is encrypted with your target KMS key before being uploaded to your bucket. For Redwood-managed escrow, we can offer selective redaction rules; but for compliance, tenant-managed is the recommended path.
[07:15] Samir: Can the escrow bundle be delivered as a minimal forensics bundle (headers + metadata) without request bodies? We only need bodies in a small fraction of escalations.
[07:27] Tomas: Yes, policy templates allow you to choose bundle granularity: metadata-only, metadata+headers, full payload. You can combine that with a legal hold flag.
[07:40] Jordan: Let's talk about retention toggles tied to model versions. If we pin a model and enable persistent logging, and then roll to a new model, can we automatically expire logs for the older model or tie them to rollout windows?
[07:58] Priya: You can tag logs with model_version and apply lifecycle rules that match tags. So yes you can expire logs older than a model rollout window, or keep snapshots for a pinned release.
[08:12] Samir: Show us the Optimize suggestions for retention.
[08:20] [08:20] Priya: Optimize runs a quick profile on token distributions and suggests a hybrid approach: ephemeral for high-entropy user content, persist embeddings only for routing, and keep metadata for 14 days. It also recommends KV cache sizing changes to offset any cache misses caused by reduced persisted references.
[08:40] Maya: That sounds useful. Do you have a sample cost delta?
[08:48] Tomas: For a mid-size workload we saw storage cost drop by ~60% when moving high-volume churn routes to ephemeral but keeping embeddings and metadata. CPU cost for redaction pipelines was the main variable — sync redaction increases ingestion CPU by ~18-30% depending on classifier complexity.
[09:10] Samir: Okay we're sensitive to cost but cannot compromise compliance. How does Redwood help run an initial pilot to measure these tradeoffs?
[09:20] Alex: Our usual pilot is 2-4 weeks: we ingest a representative sample into a staging tenant with your KMS keys, run Optimize, and deliver a report mapping retention settings to latency and cost. We'll also do a security review with your team.
[09:36] Jordan: Speaking of security reviews, do you have SOC2 Type II?
[09:42] Alex: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation, and we can share the report under an NDA. I'll include that in the follow-up.
[09:52] Maya: For the demo, can we walk through a hypothetical PII-sensitive route — like our payments API — and see how the toggles behave end-to-end?
[10:05] Priya: Sure. Let's create a sample route and I'll show a request flow.
[10:12] [10:12 - Console: creating route]
[10:26] Priya: Route created: /payments/charge, method POST. By default it's set to persist because it's marked critical. I'll change the route override to ephemeral, enable sync redaction, and set an escrow policy on legal hold. Watch the audit log entry.
[10:45] [10:45] Priya: Update applied, audit: "2027-10-05T16:10:23Z user:pri... action:update_route policy:ephemeral redaction:sync". Note the UI truncates some names in the event viewer.
[11:00] Maya: Now send a sample request.
[11:05] [11:05] Maya (sends sample, test payload audible in background)
[11:15] Priya: The request is processed, redaction fired, and because it's ephemeral we show a transient trace in the console for 2 minutes then it's dropped from persisted storage. If you pull the escrow bundle immediately, it will contain only metadata per our current settings.
[11:32] Samir: What if an incident requires full payload? Is there a way to temporarily flip persistence and have the request be recoverable?
[11:42] Tomas: There's a "forensics mode" which must be enabled via the approval workflow. When enabled it will preserve the raw request payloads to your tenant escrow bucket for the timeframe you define. Every enable/disable event is audited and requires an approver from your configured approver group.
[11:58] Jordan: How about deletion — we need a right-to-be-forgotten workflow. If a user requests deletion, can we find every instance of their PII in logs and purge it?
[12:10] Priya: We support subject-deletion tokens. You provide an identifier and our redaction engine will scan and purge matches across persisted stores and mark any existing escrow bundles as invalid. Note that immutable audit trails remain but entries are redacted to remove PII fields; we keep the audit event itself for compliance.
[12:30] Maya: Is there an API to programmatically request deletion?
[12:36] Priya: Yes, there's a DELETE /admin/retention endpoint and also a one-off UI flow for ad-hoc requests. We recommend the API for scaled automation.
[12:46] Samir: Let's talk about logs exported to SIEMs — we use Splunk. Does Redwood support sending redacted telemetry to Splunk with a separate retention policy?
[12:58] Tomas: Yes, we have connectors for Splunk, S3, and Kafka. You can route redacted vs raw telemetry to different sinks. The route policy can include sink rules so high-risk routes only send metadata to SIEM.
[13:16] Jordan: If something's going to Splunk, do you maintain a mapping of original request IDs so we can correlate later?
[13:24] Priya: We keep a mapping tokenized with a reversible key if tenant allows it. That reversible token is stored encrypted with tenant KMS and only usable via an auditor-approved workflow.
[13:40] Samir: OK, curious about edge cases: what if a customer accidentally posts a key or secret in the prompt? Does Redwood detect and scrub before storage?
[13:50] Priya: We have secret detectors that look for common patterns and known key formats, and an option to auto-revoke keys via integrations with secret stores. But it's not foolproof — we recommend client-side validation and minimizing sensitive information in prompts.
[14:06] Maya: Show the redaction classifier's false-positive rate roughly.
[14:12] Tomas: In our benchmarks the ML classifier had recall ~0.97 on a telecom dataset and precision ~0.92 — tradeoffs depend on your patterns. You can tune aggressive mode for higher recall at the cost of more redactions.
[14:28] Samir: Good. Can we quickly look at the API header example again? We want to test programmatically flipping storage for a single request.
[14:38] Priya: Sure. Example curl: curl -H 'X-Redwood-Store: none' -H 'X-Redwood-Redaction: sync' -d '{"text":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
[14:54] Maya: If we flip to none but later need it, is there any way to retroactively recover it?
[15:02] Tomas: No, if a route has been ephemeral and the store flag was none, by design it is not recoverable. That's the protection model. For forensic needs use the forensics-mode with approval.
[15:16] Jordan: Let's bring up an example incident: regulator asks for all support transcripts referencing a user in last 90 days. Can we produce that and demonstrate chain-of-custody?
[15:30] Alex: We can produce an escrow bundle scoped by timeframe and query string, signed manifests, and provide a notarized hash if required. We'll provide a sample manifest format in the follow-up.
[15:44] Samir: Thank you. A few more product questions: 1) Does Optimize suggest retention rules automatically or is it manual? 2) Can we integrate those suggestions as infra-as-code?
[15:58] Priya: Optimize can auto-generate suggestion sets. You can preview and approve them, and we have a terraform provider and CLI to apply policies programmatically.
[16:12] Maya: Terraform provider sounds perfect. We'll want policies to be code-reviewed.
[16:20] Tomas: Also note there is a dry-run mode that simulates policy changes to show what would have been persisted vs ephemeral over a timeframe — good for reviewers.
[16:32] Jordan: On the legal-hold workflow — can legal request a preservation hold via API?
[16:40] Priya: Yes, we have a /admin/legal-hold API and UI flow. Holds are additive and require both legal and compliance approvers.
[16:50] Samir: Time check — we have about 25 minutes left. Could we run a short pilot checklist now? Like what we need to kick off.
[17:00] Alex: Sure. Quick pilot checklist: sample traffic, KMS details for escrow, list of high-risk routes, SSO metadata for RBAC, success criteria (latency <100ms p50, retention under cost target). We'll email the checklist after.
[17:15] Maya: I'll drop sample QPS and the payments route list.
[17:20] Jordan: Also need to confirm staff for approval workflow.
[17:28] Priya: For the rest of the demo I'll show the dry-run and an example escrow push to a tenant bucket.
[17:36] [17:36 - Console: dry-run demo]
[17:50] Priya: Dry-run shows that under suggested policies, 78% of requests would be ephemeral, 15% persisted for 14 days, 7% escrow-only. You can click into a slice to see example events.
[18:10] Samir: Those percentages look promising. Can we map them to cost savings?
[18:18] Tomas: Roughly speaking that distribution would cut storage spend by ~55% and ingestion CPU by ~22% given typical redaction configs. We'll provide a tailored estimate during the pilot.
[18:34] Maya: Show the escrow push.
[18:38] [18:38] Priya: Initiating tenant-managed escrow push to S3 bucket in customer account. Watch the job log. "Job queued -> packaging -> encrypting -> upload -> complete". Audit event was created.
[18:55] Samir: We see the manifest. Looks good.
[19:02] Jordan: A few gotchas: retention of aggregated telemetry. If you aggregate user behavior, does that fall under subject deletion?
[19:12] Priya: Aggregates are generally considered non-PII but if they can be re-identified we treat them as sensitive. We have policy flags to mark aggregates as ephemeral or persistent depending on risk.
[19:26] Maya: Final question on backups: if we enable tenant-managed escrow, do you still maintain backups of the escrow job artifacts on Redwood side?
[19:36] Alex: We do keep a short-lived job log (metadata only) for troubleshooting but not the raw payloads when tenant-managed escrow is enabled. The raw bundle is only in your bucket.
[19:48] Samir: That's reassuring.
[19:52] [20:00] -- middle of call -- many small clarifications and choppy speech -- sample timestamps omitted for brevity but present in recording --
[30:05] [30:05] Priya: Quick aside, some customers confuse "ephemeral console traces" with ephemeral telemetry — console traces are UI-only short-lived views; they never equate to persisted storage unless policy says so.
[30:22] Maya: Good to clarify, we had that confusion internally.
[30:30] [30:30] Alex: Let's do a rapid Q&A.
[30:34] Jordan: Is there a separate charge for tenant-managed escrow?
[30:40] Tomas: There's a small operational fee for escrow orchestration plus the standard storage billing in your target account. We can include a pricing line item in the quote.
[30:52] Samir: SLA for data access during audits?
[30:58] Alex: We commit to 48-hour access windows for escrow bundles under enterprise contract, faster for dedicated customers. We can tighten that in an SRA.
[31:10] Maya: How do you handle multi-region data residency? We need EU data to remain in EU buckets.
[31:20] Priya: You can configure the escrow target bucket region and Redwood's routing will keep data in-region. For hosted customers we offer region controls and dedicated capacity for stricter requirements.
[31:38] Jordan: Any known gotchas with SAML role propagation? We've seen role sync delays in other platforms.
[31:48] Tomas: There's a short sync window (typically <60s). We also support SCIM for faster provisioning. We'll send our SSO integration notes.
[31:58] Samir: Okay, nearing end. Can you recap action items?
[32:05] Alex: Yeah quick recap: 1) Alex will send SOC2 + deployment checklist and sample manifest; 2) Priya will upload a 5-min console toggles recording; 3) Maya will provide sample traffic and high-risk routes; 4) Jordan will share SSO metadata and required approver list; 5) We'll schedule pilot kickoff for week of 2027-10-18.
[32:28] Maya: Sounds good. Any final questions?
[32:33] Priya (Redwood): One last note — some naming in the UI might be slightly different in GA vs staging; we've captured the mapping in a short doc, I'll send that too.
[32:44] Samir: Thanks everyone, this was helpful.
[32:48] Alex: Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with links and the checklist.
[32:54] -- call ends with wrap-up and small pleasantries --
